tables.caption: Table 2. Complete validation-selected parameters. QR entries are ridge penalties; KNN entries are neighborhood counts. W52 plain KNN selects the full pool at both horizons.
Table 3. Complete selected conditional menu with breach rates and same-history frozen-F contrasts. Loss is in source-specific USD millions; B1 statistics are post-result / exploratory.
Table 4. Complete selected conditional menu with breach rates and same-history frozen-F contrasts. Loss is in source-specific USD millions; B1 statistics are post-result / exploratory.
Table 5. Summary of post-result / exploratory robustness; complete numerical tables remain in the appendices.

tables.caption: Table 6. Post-result / exploratory paired predictive-accuracy tests. Negative t favors QR; normal DM and Student-reference HLN p values are two sided. Holm p uses the fixed 72 common-history family; original cross-window FX comparisons are outside it. Original primaries and legacy remain fixed.

Table 7. Post-result / exploratory coverage diagnostics. k/n counts strict breaches on the fixed H+1 grid; POF/independence/CC are chi-square-reference p values. DQ is the overlap-aware full-sample HAC adaptation. Boundary and small-sample qualifications apply.

Table 8. Post-result / exploratory parsimonious QR. Four predictors plus intercept, expanded validation penalty menu, original split/refit schedule. Percent changes compare loss against the original QR and matched F. Every original primary remains unchanged.

Table 9. All eight classical-bound plug-in L cells. Loss uses source-native units (FX USD; Treasury USD millions). Δ F/QR compares the same W and refit schedule; positive values are adverse for L. DM p is the unadjusted working-reference paired L–F test; Appendix J retains both comparators and a separate 16-member Holm family. Original primaries are unchanged.

Table 10. Complete panel summary: number of four H/W cells with lower pinball loss than matched F. These are descriptive counts, not independent trials or evidence selected after screening losses. Appendix K retains every loss change and breach count.

Table 11. Fixed FHS, GARCH-scaled peak-headroom POT and true leaf-distribution QRF on all original cells. Each entry gives Δ loss% versus matched frozen F / strict breaches; negative Δ favors the new method. NA retains a failed or structurally ineligible complete-cell comparison; issued counts are not scored as partial successes. Full native losses, reasons and comparisons are in Appendix L.
Table A1. Artificial coherent continuations. Symbols are constructed quantities, not source-record estimates.

Table A2. Completed H=1 windows from one artificial history, in arbitrary position units. P is the native peak, G the native headroom and T the peak after reanchoring at x=2. These values are not source-record estimates.
Table B1. Complete original mean loss grid. Δ is the stored paired mean F minus S; negative favors F within that setting.

Table B2. Complete earlier retrieval-extension mean loss menu and same-set F-minus-S paired mean, in source-reported USD millions. Full 720 rows repeat original references. Differences are computed before display rounding.

Table D1. Original QR/KNN/scaled-KNN horizon-coherence diagnostics; the later AR addition is not included. A crossing means stored C(H6)>C(H24), with no tolerance used to redefine the event. Maximum gap is displayed in USD millions (FX divided by 10⁶; Treasury already in that unit). The distinct financial quantities are not pooled.

Table D2. All 56 late fixed-terminal evidence diagnostics, rounded to three significant figures; * marks an exact crossing of the fixed 1120 reference threshold. Treasury is the separately fitted Treasury aggregate; F/S/K are the matched frozen controls. A noncrossing is not coverage certification, and evidence magnitude is not a financial-quality ranking. All 896 phase rows and exact rational identities are retained in the supplement.

Table D3. Complete post-inspection ordinary empirical-rank ablation. Percentages are QR-minus-I and I-minus-F mean-loss changes relative to the right report; negative favors the left. QR means and counts are imported unchanged from the original selected fits. I/F counts are newly reconstructed; columns list I/F/QR strict breaches over 6,625 FX or 277 Treasury origins. H counts source records. Sources are not pooled.
Table E1. All eight full-origin frontiers among the same eight fixed reports; 6,625 FX or 277 Treasury origins per row. Units are source native and are never pooled.
Table E2. All eight existing globally anchored H+1 sparse-grid frontiers. Counts are FX 947/265 and Treasury 40/12 for H6/H24. These are descriptive sensitivities with shared training histories.

Table F1. Complete conditional loss menu and same-history frozen controls on 6,625 FX origins, in USD millions. Every selected QR/KNN/scaled cell is shown. Rolling and one-state reference results and all breach/severity quantities remain in the complete CSVs.

Table F2. Complete selected conditional loss menu and same-history frozen controls on 277 Treasury origins. Losses are in the source's USD-million units, not FX USD. H6/H24 mean six/24 weekly transitions. No monetary average is pooled across sources.

Table F3. Complete later AR comparison. Entries are within-reference mean-loss percentages; negative favors AR. S/F have matching source, H, W and refit schedule; QR is the original selected same-cell fit. Counts are AR / S strict breaches over 6,625 FX or 277 Treasury origins. Every row is exploratory; sources are not pooled.

Table F4. Preference sensitivity of the four named fixed comparisons. Differences are left minus right. FX amounts are divided by 10⁶; Treasury amounts already have USD-million source units. The sources and economic horizons are not pooled. ω is the stipulated shortfall/excess weight ratio; equality holds at a finite displayed crossing, before rounding. Reference definitions remain those of Section 5.
Table H1. Murphy full-breakpoint audit for both original primaries. The extrema of left-minus-right elementary scores span zero in both cases. Integral agreement is an arithmetic identity check.

Table H2. Complete fixed 72-member common-history Holm family, including nonsignificant and identical-loss rows. Comparators F/S/K are frozen with the displayed common W. Negative t favors the conditional method. The .05 decision is based on unrounded normal-reference DM p values and Holm adjustment; it is an exploratory working-reference decision conditional on valid component tests. Identical losses retain their NA t/status and bookkeeping p=1.

Table I1. Treasury selected C2 coefficients and effects. Norms are in standardized/response-normalized coordinates. Mean absolute projected slope effect is in source USD millions. Loss changes are descriptive and all adverse F comparisons are retained.

Table I2. Pointwise C2 comparisons with I and F. Max |Δ| is capacity difference in source USD millions; ρC includes the shared issue floor, ρG removes it. J is strict-breach-set Jaccard. Hits show C2/reference and XOR counts discordant breach occasions.

Table J1. Original positive-increment-AR oracle-quantile simulation, retained unchanged. Rates/SE are percentages; Δ5 is percentage points from 5%. Endpoint tails are evaluated at the same threshold. Every specified cell is retained.

Table J2. Every post-result / exploratory L comparison. Negative t/Δloss favors L. Holm uses only this new 16-comparison family; the original 72-member family is unchanged. Component p values are approximate working references with shared-training and post-inspection limitations.

Table J3. Corrected primary simulation cases. Each row uses 100000 independent paths and includes the issue position in the peak. Rate/SE/endpoint are percentages; Δ5 is percentage points from 5%. Level rows use the stationary-marginal endpoint quantile; increment rows use their own known endpoint quantile with a zero starting position. Stat. denotes a stationary random start; Abs95 is the absolute-level 95th percentile. End measures the absolute change from the issue position exceeding the endpoint threshold. All seeds and exact counts are retained in the correction CSV.

Table J4. All prespecified anchor-definition and conditional-endpoint-oracle sensitivities. Each row has 100000 paths. Signed95 is the signed-level 95th percentile, while Abs95 is the absolute-level 95th percentile. Marginal/conditional thresholds on a given path cell share the same seed; these are not independent replications. Full seeds, endpoint rates, SE and exact parameters remain in simulation.csv.

Table K1. All 48 panel H/W cells, no favorable selection. F loss is in source USD millions; the next columns are percentage loss changes relative to F. Hits list F/QR33/C2/L, respectively. All methods complete on277 evaluation origins in every cell.

Table L1. All 24 planned method cells. Loss is native FX USD or Treasury USD millions. Failed complete cells have NA, regardless of earlier issued reports; no partial average substitutes for the full evaluation.

Table L2. All 48 planned paired comparisons. Tests are post-result working references; NA component tests remain NA. A separate 48-slot Holm family reserves missing/degenerate slots as 1 for adjustment only. This is distinct from claiming an observed valid p value of 1. Negative Δ/t favors the new method; shared training and inspected outcomes limit interpretation.

Table L3. Every retained NA classification. For boundary fits, δ is fitted persistence minus one and ε is excess over the declared numerical ceiling; optimizer flag 0 denotes success. Strict-tail structural exclusions have no fitted persistence. No missing full-cell loss is imputed.
